feedback: Approved for racing, unchanged. The candidate restores wheel_track to 0.12 and changes mass 0.8 to 0.5 kg and body_length 0.16 to 0.12 m, which lowers yaw inertia by the stated formula. The other fields (kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.0, the sensor layout at y 0.08 with x ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, line_loss last_direction) match the best-supported settings. Iteration 3 (724.5) and iteration 4 (719.4) were near-identical, and iteration 5 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 did not help the slalom (progress 0.68 against about 0.67) and cost one s-bend finish. So the wheel_track hypothesis is already settled, and this candidate tests the inertia hypothesis on a clean base. Nothing is obviously broken: all values are inside the contract ranges, and the iteration 5 oval at speed 1.0 (2.10 s) leaves time margin. Its main untested risk is traction loss from the lighter mass, which the race will show. Read the race in this order: slalom progress and completions, then completion_time and completion on the oval and s-bend, then line_loss_events and steering_oscillation. Decide the next step from those numbers.
requested_changes: If the slalom still ends off_track with progress below 0.75 while the oval and s-bend finish under 2.8 s, try base_speed 0.9 with the inertia change kept. Iteration 3 to 5 show slalom progress is stuck near 0.63 to 0.68 at speeds 1.0 to 1.1, so speed is the lever not yet isolated.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 (iteration 3 slalom 0.33, s-bend 0.20 to 0.25), raise kd from 1.0 to 1.2 with kp kept at 4.5, rather than changing kp. Iteration 4 showed raising kp to 5.0 added oscillation on the s-bend without a slalom gain.

If the oval or s-bend stops finishing, line_loss_events rise above the iteration 3 level (about 0.9 to 1.0 per run), or the robot slips at the start, restore mass to 0.8 and keep body_length 0.12. This isolates whether the mass drop, not the length change, caused the problem.
